svg.title: The invisibility gate
svg.desc: A candidate bait must pass three automated tests before it may enter the library: the rendered post-JavaScript output must be unchanged, functionality must be unchanged, and added latency must be statistically equivalent by a TOST test against a pre-registered margin. A bait failing any one of the three is deleted rather than repaired; one that passes all three enters the library with a certificate on record.
svg.text: The invisibility gate — built before any bait exists
This is the single most important safety mechanism in the project: it decides whether the whole idea is viable. A bait that leaks into
normal user experience does not merely weaken the results — it invalidates the central claim that provoking is safe.
candidate bait
TEST 1 · RENDERED OUTPUT
post-JS DOM and visible text identical to the no-bait page
TEST 2 · FUNCTION
every form submits, every link works, every API response parses
TEST 3 · TIMING
added latency equivalent by TOST against a pre-registered margin
fails any one
passes all three
deleted, not repaired
a bait that looks planted warns the
attacker that the site is defended
enters the library
with a passing certificate on record —
the runtime refuses uncertified bait
The raw response bytes must differ — that is the mechanism. Invisibility is a claim about the rendered page, the functionality and the timing.
The JSON-field bait is invisible to the application's own client, not to an arbitrary parser — a limitation worth owning before a reviewer finds it.
